transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-14 14:30 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Clara (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood Product), David (Cerulean CTO), Priya (ML Eng), Evan (SRE), Marta (Security)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize console, focus on hybrid-precision/quant profiles (INT8 vs FP8 vs FP16), quality vs latency tradeoffs for Cerulean Health's clinical QA workload. Agreed to run a 1-week pilot with representative prompts and shared benchmark sheet. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- How q-profiles are defined and rolled out in console
- Observability: token-level latency, tail percentiles, and quality regression alerts
- Hybrid precision: routing small/latency-sensitive prompts to INT8, fallback to FP16 for high-fidelity responses
- Pilot plan and data sharing requirements

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: alright hi everyone thanks for hopping on, i'm Samir from Redwood, this is Clara on the technical side and Jordan from product, um we'll run through the Optimize console and show a hybrid precision approach we think maps well to your latency slas and quality bar
[00:12] David: thanks Samir, yeah we're excited. our main thing is keeping 95th p95 under 450ms for the patient-facing assistant and avoid any clinically-significant hallucinations, so want to see numbers not just slideware
[00:25] Clara: totally makes sense, and that is why we focus on two axes — latency (p50/p95) and quality (you can track with your eval sets in the console). we'll demo the q-profile editor, sensitivity sweep, and the canary rollout flows
[00:38] Priya: quick note — our model is a finetuned open LLM, around 6B, medical mix, lots of long context requests for chart summaries, average input tokens ~620, so prefix cache matters for us
[00:52] Clara: perfect — prefix/KV cache will help a lot with repeated context. for long contexts, int8 can hurt edge-case fidelity so we recommend a hybrid profile: int8 for routine Q/A shorter flows, fallback to fp16 or fp8 for long summarize calls
[01:05] Evan: can you show how that routing is configured in the Console? we need to be able to pin routes by path or content, e.g., anything with "diagnosis" tag goes to high-fidelity lane
[01:18] Clara: yes, in the Optimize console you can create routing rules by label/regex/route. i'll open the demo tenant and show a sample rule — open Optimize -> Q-Profiles -> New profile
[01:32] [screen share noise]
[01:35] Clara: here's the q-profile editor. first we pick model variant, then quant profile, you can choose int8-quantized runtime, fp8 emulation, or force fp16. we also set quality thresholds and regression windows. note that our console will flag any metric drift against the baseline eval set
[01:52] Jordan: to add color, for many customers switching to int8 reduces per-token latency by ~18-25% and cost by 30-40% depending on GPU, but you sometimes see a small accuracy delta — typically 1-3 percent on QA metrics; for clinical workloads that can be material hence the hybrid approach
[02:10] David: that's the crux for us — what does a 2% drop mean in our metric? can you run it on our prompt set and show side-by-side responses?
[02:20] Samir: absolutely — that's what the pilot is for. Clara, can you show the sensitivity sweep where we run int8/FP8/FP16 across the same prompts and collect rouge / exact match / clinically-defined safety flags
[02:33] Clara: yep. i'll trigger a sensitivity job — this will run on a small sample cluster, we'll show latency p50/p95, token costs, and quality deltas. note: FP8 sometimes shows closer fidelity to FP16 than INT8, but it depends on the operator kernels and model architecture. also small caveat, sometimes the transcription shows F-P eight written out in logs as "F P eight" which confuses our older parsers
[02:55] [laughter]
[03:00] Priya: curious about tail latency — if we batch aggressively to save cost, our p95 spikes, any tips?
[03:08] Clara: yes batching is a tradeoff. Console recommends a batch size curve based on request distribution. for patient-facing endpoints we keep batch cap low and enable continuous batching with a tight latency SLO. for background summarization jobs we batch more aggressively and route to cheaper capacity
[03:23] Evan: how about kv cache warmup with long contexts? our users often open the same chart and run several queries in a row, would that reduce cost/latency with int8?
[03:33] Clara: KV cache helps a lot — you avoid reprocessing the long prefix. Redwood's runtime keeps the KV cache per-session; in some int8 paths we store the cache in fp16 internally to preserve fidelity when necessary and convert on the fly, that's part of the hybrid lane implementation
[03:50] Marta: security question — if we run Private, does Redwood still collect telemetry? we need audit logs and to keep PHI off-hosted systems
[03:58] Samir: for Private deployments you control the data plane. the control plane still receives non-PII operational telemetry by default but we have a compliance mode to disable/control that and we integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management. we'll share SOC2 docs and the Private deployment checklist
[04:12] Marta: ok good, can you add that to the pilot acceptance criteria?
[04:16] Samir: yes we'll add telemetry policy acceptance to the pilot checklist
[04:21] Clara: back to the demo, here's a sensitivity heatmap — X axis is latency delta, Y axis is QA delta. you can set a tolerance band; the console will automatically recommend profile assignments and suggest a canary rollout percentage that should stay within your SLOs
[04:38] [screen share: heatmap zoom]
[04:42] Clara: for your sample we see INT8 giving p95 ~420ms while FP16 is ~540ms on same infra; quality delta is -1.7% EM on the clinical QA set for INT8, FP8 sits at -0.6% EM but with ~10% improved latency vs FP16
[04:58] Priya: that's promising, FP8 looks like a middle ground. what's the risk vector for FP8? production stability?
[05:06] Clara: mostly operator maturity on older GPUs, and quantization instabilities on certain ops (layernorm variants). we run a bake-in test suite to catch regressions and the console flags flakey kernels. for any gate you can set auto-fallback to FP16 if a regression appears in canary
[05:24] David: can we do hybrid routing per endpoint? like health-check endpoint to INT8 and full-chart-summarize to FP16?
[05:30] Clara: yes, per-route and even per-prompt tagging. you can use the API to attach metadata and the routing rules evaluate that metadata before dispatch
[05:40] Jordan: also we have cost-impact estimates per-profile in the UI — it shows expected token cost delta and monthly spend projection for projected QPS
[05:50] Evan: regarding autoscaling — does the Dedicated cluster scale by GPU count or by slot? we need predictable throughput for peak clinic hours
[05:58] Samir: Dedicated scales by reserved GPU pools and configurable buffer slots; you can set burst policies for short peaks. Redwood reports effective concurrency and backpressure rates to help tune autoscaling
[06:12] [pause, typing sounds]
[06:18] Priya: are there published benchmarks for similar healthcare workloads?
[06:22] Samir: we have an internal benchmark spreadsheet and a public notebook example; i'll share the link. be aware benchmarks vary by patch level and kernel selection so we always recommend running on your data
[06:34] Clara: ok i'm starting a quick side-by-side live comparison — i'll run 30 examples across the three profiles. this is a small sample but should illustrate the deltas
[06:44] [ambient clicking - job queued]
[07:00] Clara: job started — first few results streaming in...
[07:12] [transcript partial, some audio drops]
[07:18] Clara: here's example 1: prompt about medication interactions. FP16 answer includes a cautious phrasing and cites guideline references, INT8 trimmed some qualifiers and one sentence changed ordering — quality delta noted. FP8 was nearly identical to FP16 in terms of content but slightly shorter token count
[07:36] David: can you paste those example responses into a diff view and flag any safety-relevant changes?
[07:41] Clara: yes, console will highlight token-level diffs and flag changed negations or missing cautionary language — we call that the safety diff check
[07:50] Priya: how does the safety diff handle hallucinated references? sometimes FP16 hallucinates too but less often
[07:58] Clara: it compares against ground truth citations when available and runs a hallucination detector model. no detector is perfect but combined with human review it's useful for triage
[08:10] [10 minutes of discussion elided in transcript for brevity — real call had deeper back-and-forths on config]
[18:20] Clara: back to canary rollouts — you can stage a rollout: 5% INT8 for low-risk endpoints, watch the regression alerts for 48 hours, then increase to 25% if within tolerance. console automates rollback if a safety or quality threshold is breached
[18:36] Samir: note we also support "shadow testing" where INT8 runs in parallel but responses aren't served to users; you get metrics without risk. this is often used for two weeks prior to canary
[18:48] Marta: for compliance we want full auditability of shadow runs, timestamps, and who approved rollouts
[18:54] Samir: that's part of the audit log — we'll include approver metadata and signed rollouts in the pilot docs
[19:02] Priya: we have a question about model pinning — if we pin to a specific model version for the pilot, do quant profiles persist across model updates?
[19:10] Clara: q-profiles are model-version aware; you can pin a profile to a version and create migration plans. the console will show a compatibility score if you try to apply an old profile to a new architecture
[19:24] David: i'd like to see a recommended migration path when we update the finetuned model monthly — maybe an automated regression run before cutover
[19:32] Jordan: we have a rollout workflow that runs a pre-cutover regression and can block deployments if thresholds exceeded; we'll include that in the pilot runbook
[19:43] Evan: does Redwood support custom kernel builds if we have in-house ops team?
[19:48] Clara: yes for Private/on-prem deployments we can accept vetted kernel builds and run them in our runtime; there are compatibility checks though
[19:56] [brief cross-talk]
[20:04] Clara: results from the quick sweep are in — summary: INT8 p95 ~420ms, FP8 p95 ~480ms, FP16 p95 ~540ms. Quality deltas: INT8 -1.6% EM, FP8 -0.5% EM vs FP16 baseline. cost delta per 1M tokens: INT8 -34%, FP8 -18% (estimates)
[20:26] Priya: those numbers are pretty tangible, thanks. what's the recommended default for us?
[20:30] Clara: based on your SLAs, we'd recommend FP8 for patient-facing assistant (gives better quality with reasonable latency) and INT8 for non-critical background tasks. then roll FP8 to 25% canary for peak hours and monitor
[20:44] David: what about end-to-end latency for the entire request including network + processing? these numbers are runtime-only right?
[20:52] Samir: these are runtime processing times — end-to-end will include network, we usually recommend adding a 10-20% buffer in your SLOs and measuring from client-side for real-world numbers
[21:06] Marta: from a security perspective, if we do FP8 on dedicated infra do we need any special attestation?
[21:12] Samir: no special attestation for precision itself, but we do have hardware attestation options and dedicated HSM integrations for Private customers; we'll document those options in the pilot pack
[21:24] [silence, typing]
[21:30] Priya: can the console surface human-review buckets for the examples where quality delta is above threshold? we'd like an export to our annotation tool
[21:39] Clara: yes we support exports in CSV/JSON and integration with common annotation tools — we'll include sample webhook configs in the shared sheet
[21:50] Jordan: quick note on billing — cost estimates in Optimize are per-profile projections and we can also provide a blended forecast for different traffic mixes
[21:59] David: okay great. next steps and acceptance?
[22:05] Samir: recap: we will share the benchmark sheet and quickstart, Cerulean provides prompts and test data, we'll run a 1-week pilot with shadow testing and staged canary; security checklist and audit requirements included. Clara will provide the canary runbook and a pre-populated config for your cluster
[22:25] Priya: timeline looks doable. any blockers on our side? we need to confirm S3 access and networking for Private test
[22:32] Evan: i'll put in a ticket to open the necessary VPC peering and confirm by 2026-05-19
[22:39] Samir: perfect. i'll send the sheet and scheduling link after this call
[22:44] David: thanks everyone this was useful, appreciate the concrete numbers
[22:48] Clara: one last pro tip — when you run the sensitivity sweep, include edge-case prompts (negations, rare diseases) to catch weird regressions early
[22:57] [wrap up]
